churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, transport, and config are each behind one well-defined module, so framework or API moves touch few files; the missing strict mode and near-zero test coverage are what keep refactors riskier than they should be.

findings.issue: TypeScript strict mode is not enabled (no strict/strictNullChecks), deviating from the CLI scaffold default; the extensive null-union types in shared/models.ts are decorative without it.
findings.suggestion: Set "strict": true in tsconfig.json (v22 already defaults strictTemplates on) and fix any surfaced null-safety issues.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but never imported anywhere in src/.
Uses the pre-v22 @Injectable() idiom; Angular 22 ships @Service({autoProvided: false}) plus an official migration schematic (ng generate @angular/core:service).
Client /_data fetches are not abortable; rapid navigation leaves stale in-flight requests and cache entries.
findings.suggestion: Thread an AbortController (abort previous request per path) into the fetch and clean up on abort.

findings.issue: Test coverage is minimal — only the pure formatting helpers are tested; the filtering, pagination and sorting logic in home.ts and move-table.ts has no safety net for future changes.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for the filter/sort/pagination computeds in home.ts and move-table.ts.

findings.issue: The title strategy is coupled to the resolver output via the magic string 'vm' (and a data['notFound'] flag).
findings.suggestion: Export a shared constant or route-data interface shared with app.routes.ts.

findings.issue: Manual router.events subscription with hand-rolled previous-URL tracking and DestroyRef teardown in the constructor.
findings.suggestion: Use takeUntilDestroyed() from @angular/core/rxjs-interop (or an afterRenderEffect) for terser, harder-to-misuse teardown.

findings.issue: @types/node ^22 while the app runs on Node 24 (root .nvmrc: 24.22.1).
findings.suggestion: Bump @types/node to ^24 to match the runtime.

summary: This is a current-generation Angular 22 codebase that would survive framework updates with minimal churn: v22-stable APIs throughout (Service decorator, BootstrapContext, RESPONSE_INIT, signals-first components, zoneless), a platform-first data layer of raw fetch + URL behind a single well-defined PageData/loader module, and a deliberate compact-view-model architecture that keeps the browser away from the large raw API documents. The main forward-looking gaps are the absent TypeScript strict mode (all those null-union types are unenforced), the unused @angular/forms dependency, and near-zero test coverage over the filtering/sorting logic.
